references.text: The waters of the Red Sea parted in a similar way when Moses stretched out his hand, and the Israelites crossed on dry ground. Both texts describe God's miraculous control over water.
The waters of the Red Sea returned to their place after the Israelites had crossed, just as the Jordan River here returned to its normal state.
This is the preceding account of how the priests carried the ark of the covenant down into the Jordan and the waters stopped, making possible the crossing that is completed in chapter 4.
The priests stood in the middle of the Jordan with the ark while the people hurried across, providing context for when they finally stepped up out of the river.
The Jordan overflowed all its banks during harvest time but stopped when the feet of the priests touched the water. This explains the natural state to which the waters returned.
Elijah and Elisha crossed the Jordan on dry ground when Elijah struck the water with his cloak, a similar miraculous water crossing.
